hints: Relate acceleration/deceleration to the gradient of a line on a velocity-time graph: $\text{gradient} = \frac{\Delta v}{\Delta t}$.
The particle decelerates from speed $V$ to $0\text{ m s}^{-1}$ over a time interval of $6\text{ s}$ at a magnitude of $\frac{5}{3}\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Set up the equation $0 = V - \left(\frac{5}{3}\right)(6)$ and solve for $V$.
walkthrough:
Use the definition of acceleration as the slope of the velocity-time graph over the deceleration interval from $t = 4$ to $t = 10$:
$$\text{gradient} = \frac{0 - V}{10 - 4} = -\frac{5}{3}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
On a velocity-time graph, acceleration is represented by the gradient (slope) of the line segment:
$$\text{gradient} = \frac{v - u}{t}$$

During the second stage from $t = 4\text{ s}$ to $t = 10\text{ s}$, the time interval is:
$$\Delta t = 10 - 4 = 6\text{ s}$$
The particle starts this interval with speed $V$ and comes to instantaneous rest, so its final velocity is $0\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

The rate of deceleration is given as $\frac{5}{3}\text{ m s}^{-2}$, which means the acceleration is $-\frac{5}{3}\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$a = \frac{0 - V}{6} = -\frac{5}{3}$$

Multiply both sides by $-6$:
$$V = 6 \times \frac{5}{3} = 2 \times 5 = 10\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

ai_rubric.Interpreting Motion Graphs: Uses $0 = V - (5/3)(10 - 4)$ or gradient to obtain $V = 10$.

hints: The total distance travelled is represented by the total area between the velocity-time graph and the time axis (treating all areas as positive).
Calculate the area of the forward journey from $t = 0$ to $t = 10$ using the triangle area formula $\frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height}$ with base $10$ and height $V = 10$.
Subtract this forward distance from the total distance $68\text{ m}$ to find the distance of the reverse journey, and solve $\frac{1}{2}(T - 10)(3) = 18$ for $T$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the distance travelled in the first $10\text{ s}$ as the area of the first triangle with base $10\text{ s}$ and height $V = 10\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$s_1 = \frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 10 = 50\text{ m}$$

The remaining distance for the return journey between $t = 10$ and $t = T$ has maximum speed $3\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$s_2 = 68 - 50 = 18\text{ m}$$

Express $s_2$ as the area of the second triangle with base $T - 10$ and height $3\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$\frac{1}{2} \times (T - 10) \times 3 = 18 \implies \frac{3}{2}(T - 10) = 18$$
$$T - 10 = 18 \times \frac{2}{3} = 12 \implies T = 22\text{ s}$$
teacher_walkthrough: On a velocity-time graph, distance travelled is given by the area enclosed by the graph and the time axis. Total distance is the sum of the magnitudes of all enclosed areas.

The motion consists of two distinct triangular phases:
1. Forward motion from $t = 0$ to $t = 10\text{ s}$.
2. Reverse motion from $t = 10\text{ s}$ to $t = T\text{ s}$.

Calculate the area of the first triangle (forward phase):
$$\text{base}_1 = 10 - 0 = 10\text{ s}$$
$$\text{height}_1 = V = 10\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
$$\text{Area}_1 = \frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 10 = 50\text{ m}$$

The total distance travelled across the entire journey is given as $68\text{ m}$. Calculate the distance travelled in the reverse phase:
$$\text{Area}_2 = 68 - \text{Area}_1 = 68 - 50 = 18\text{ m}$$

The second triangle represents motion back towards O with a peak speed of $3\text{ m s}^{-1}$, base duration $(T - 10)\text{ s}$, and height $3\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$\text{Area}_2 = \frac{1}{2} \times (T - 10) \times 3$$

ai_rubric.Interpreting Motion Graphs: Finds distance in first $10\text{ s}$ is $50\text{ m}$, sets up $(1/2)(T - 10)(3) + 50 = 68$, and solves to find $T = 22$.
